correctness.rationale: The Petersen graph is specified by 15 explicit edges on vertices 0..9 and independently as KG(5,2). verify_petersen.py exhaustively enumerated all 331 nonempty matchings with f-vector (15,75,145,90,6), formed 160 disjoint codimension-one matched pairs (14,61,79,6 by lower dimension), and checked acyclicity via all 975 directed Hasse incidences and a topological ordering of all 331 faces. The resulting critical cells are one dimension-0 cell, five dimension-2 cells and five dimension-3 cells. For each critical 3-cell the exact signed gradient-path recurrence yields zero coefficients on all five critical 2-cells. The 2-skeleton is a wedge of five S^2; pi_2 to integral H_2 is an isomorphism, making every 3-cell attaching map null. The independent KG(5,2) implementation gives the same f-vector and modular boundary ranks (14,61,79,6) over p=2,3,5,7,11. Finite-field tests are cross-checks only; the signed integral Morse boundary and Hurewicz argument support the homotopy conclusion.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical nonplanar, symmetric cubic graph. Its ordinary matching complex is a natural invariant in a class where exact homotopy types are generally difficult. The determination of both sphere dimensions and their exact multiplicities, including the integral vanishing of all attaching coefficients, provides a concrete non-outerplanar topology benchmark beyond numerical face counts, Euler characteristic, connectivity, or field-valued homology. The result is a meaningful exact homotopy classification of a named object, while avoiding unsupported family-wide claims.
